messages:
maya: Quick check — can someone run a short perf run in DC1 (airgapped/private) against main with the q8 weights? Need latency and peak GPU memory at seq=512 and seq=2048 to validate parity vs hosted. TL;DR: 1) seq512 + seq2048, 2) single-stream (batch=1), 3) 100 warmup + 500 measured iters. Put results in the shared sheet and ping me. Thanks.

samir: Got it — which namespace & model exactly? also which binary (we have runtime v1.14 and v1.15 on different nodes).

maya: Use namespace `infra-inference`, model `redwood-v2-7b-q8`. Prefer runtime v1.15 if available, but note both if not. Bench script is at: https://git.local/bench/perf_bench.py (private link). Quick command: `python perf_bench.py --model redwood-v2-7b-q8 --seq 512 --batch 1 --warmup 100 --iters 500 --namespace infra-inference`

dmitri: FYI DC1 machines still have SMT enabled on some racks — might skew latency tail. If you see odd jitter, try disabling HT for the run or pin threads: `echo 0 > /sys/devices/system/cpu/smt/control` (requires reboot). Also capture `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv -l 1` during the run.

li: Also capture these system details so we can compare: kernel (uname -a), NIC driver (ethtool -i <iface>), and offload settings (`ethtool -k <iface>`). If the NIC has GRO/TSO offload differences vs hosted, that changes perf.

emily: I can run this on node-cc-07 around 10:30 PT today. I have access to infra-inference. @maya — should I do both runtime versions on the same node or use a different node for v1.14?

maya: Thanks emily — if possible run v1.15 on node-cc-07 and v1.14 on node-cc-08 so we avoid noisy restarts. If you only have one node, do sequential runs but annotate which runtime in the sheet. Link to results sheet: https://docs.local/rdw/dc1-perf-q2 (internal).

emily: ACK. I will also dump flamegraph samples if tail looks bad: `perf record -F 99 -g -- sleep 60` + `perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded && flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg`. Will attach artifacts.

samir: Quick question — should I use KV cache warmup? the prod hosted bench uses 8 tokens prefix warmup. maya: Use the same workload as prod where possible — enable KV cache warmup of 8 tokens. Include both cold-start and warmed runs (mark them in the sheet).

oncall-bot: Reminder: DC1 maintenance window 1782504000-1782507600 UTC; if run overlaps please ping @eng-sre.

maya: Good catch — try to finish before the maintenance window or coordinate with eng-sre. If you hit infra issues, tag `#eng-sre` and drop outputs in the sheet. After runs, please note any config diffs vs hosted (kernel, offloads, runtime flags, quant backend).

emily: Will run now and report back with a brief summary + artifacts (flame.svg, nvidia-smi log, uname, ethtool outputs).

dmitri: If anyone else runs later and sees >10% tail latency regression vs hosted, stop and ping me — I'll triage core scheduling/NUMA.

maya: Thanks all — this will help the parity checklist for Private deployments.
